stances.claim: Under Velarde v. Social Justice Party (April 28, 2004), the dispositive portion controls who won; here, the petitions were 'DISMISSED for being moot,' so the respondents (executive branch) formally won.
stances.rhetorical_move: Doctrinal anchoring -- quotes the controlling rule then applies it cleanly.

stances.claim: The extensive 'guideline' language about continuing ICC cooperation obligation is obiter dicta -- not binding, not citable as precedent.
stances.rhetorical_move: Adopts Harry Roque's procedural framing on the binding/non-binding distinction.

stances.claim: Notwithstanding non-binding status, the Leonen decision was 'probably signaling' that a future live, non-moot petition would meet a Court ready to uphold the obiter.
stances.rhetorical_move: Reads Court tea leaves; explicit predictive forecast.
stances.confidence: medium -- qualified as 'probably,' framed as 'in my humble view'

stances.claim: Retired Justice Vicente V. Mendoza's UP-forum complaint that the decision is a 'mere advisory opinion' barred by the Court's Internal Rules has substantial merit and should be reckoned with.
stances.rhetorical_move: Quotes a respected critic without fully adopting the position.

stances.claim: Petitioners' failure to file before the Philippine withdrawal became a 'fait accompli' is the dispositive procedural defect; future petitions framed under proper justiciability requirements remain open.
stances.rhetorical_move: Identifies the operative procedural lesson for future litigators.
stances.confidence: high -- direct application of the decision text

one_paragraph_summary: After Pangilinan v. Cayetano (March 16, 2021) issued -- and after the Court's March 16 press release, the July 21 text release of the 101-page unanimous decision, and the Senate's July 22 press release -- both petitioners and respondents claimed victory. CJ Panganiban adjudicates the conflict by applying Velarde v. Social Justice Party (April 28, 2004): the dispositive portion controls. Because the petitions were 'DISMISSED for being moot,' the respondents -- Executive Secretary Medialdea and Foreign Secretary Locsin -- formally won. The extended discussion that delighted the senators -- that the Philippines remains bound to cooperate on ICC proceedings initiated before the March 16, 2019 withdrawal, and that the President 'is subject to the Constitution and existing statute' -- is obiter dicta, not binding precedent, as Presidential Spokesperson Harry Roque correctly noted. CJ then offers a qualified forecast 'in my humble view': the unanimous, no-separate-opinions Leonen ponencia 'was probably signaling' that a future live, non-moot petition would meet a Court ready to uphold the obiter. He amplifies the complaint via retired Justice Vicente V. Mendoza at a UP forum -- 'it is not a decision; it is a mere advisory opinion' barred by the Court's Internal Rules -- without fully adopting the harsher framing. The procedural lesson for future litigators is the dispositive lesson of the case: petitioners should have filed before the Philippine withdrawal became a 'fait accompli,' and any successor petition must 'conform to the basic requisites of justiciability.' Substantively, the column rests on Fatou Bensouda's war-on-drugs murder finding (July 1, 2016 - March 16, 2019, possibly reaching back to Nov. 1, 2011) -- material CJ treats more fully in his June 27 column.
